title_en: Guizhou Huading Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. v. China Southern Power Grid Co., Ltd., Ultra High Voltage Transmission Company, et al. — dispute over property rights protection
ruling_gist_en: After the approval of mineral resource overlay, if the construction unit adjusts the engineering route causing overlay of mineral resources outside the original approved scope, the legal effect of the original approval cannot extend to the new overlay act, and the construction unit shall re-apply for overlay approval. However, if the route adjustment is indeed based on public interest, and the adjusted route has been timely submitted to the natural resources administrative department without the intention to circumvent the mineral resource overlay approval, it may be determined in light of the actual circumstances that the construction unit does not constitute infringement.

full_text_en:
Guiding Case No. [Not applicable] — Guizhou Huading Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. v. China Southern Power Grid Co., Ltd. Ultra High Voltage Transmission Company et al. — dispute over property rights protection

【Ruling Summary】

Where, after approval of mineral resource overlay, the construction entity adjusts the project route, causing overlay of mineral resources beyond the originally approved scope, the legal effect of the original approval does not extend to the new overlay act, and the construction entity shall re-submit the overlay for approval. However, if the route adjustment is genuinely based on public interest, and the adjusted route has been promptly submitted to the competent natural resources administrative department without intent to circumvent the approval procedure for mineral resource overlay, the construction entity may be found not to constitute infringement in light of the actual circumstances.

The mineral rights enjoyed by a mining right holder over newly increased reserves during the exercise of mining rights do not originate from the time the original mining rights were established, and shall be obtained by the mining right holder only after payment of the transfer consideration separately in accordance with law. In the case of mineral resource overlay, the mining rights of the mining right holder over the newly increased reserves after the occurrence of the overlay fact are posterior property rights compared to the property rights of the construction entity over the project. Where the mining right holder claims compensation for losses of such newly increased reserves, the People's Court shall not support it.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2020) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 1217

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Guizhou Huading Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. Domicile: Beside Guibi Road, Yachi Town, Qixingguan District, Bijie City, Guizhou Province.

Legal Representative: Rui Xiaoyong, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Yang Weimin, Lawyer of Guizhou Weishengdao Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Lu Jiao, Lawyer of Guizhou Weishengdao Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): China Southern Power Grid Co., Ltd. Ultra High Voltage Transmission Company. Domicile: No. 223, Kexue Avenue, High-tech Industrial Development Zone, Huangpu District, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

Person in Charge: Niu Baohong, Deputy General Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Hu Nan, Lawyer of Beijing Junhe Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Zou Delong, Lawyer of Beijing Junhe Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): China Southern Power Grid Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 11, Kexiang Road, Science City, Luogang District, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Meng Zhenping, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Deng Chengjun, Lawyer of Grandall Law Firm (Guiyang).

In the case of dispute over property rights protection between appellant Guizhou Huading Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company) and appellant China Southern Power Grid Co., Ltd. Ultra High Voltage Transmission Company (hereinafter referred to as Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company) and respondent China Southern Power Grid Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Southern Power Grid Company), Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company appealed against the civil judgment (2018) Qian Min Chu No. 98 rendered by the Guizhou High People's Court. The Supreme People's Court, after accepting the case on October 20, 2020, formed a collegial panel and held a hearing in accordance with law. The agents ad litem of appellant Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company, Yang Weimin and Lu Jiao, the agents ad litem of appellant Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company, Hu Nan and Zou Delong, and the agent ad litem of respondent Southern Power Grid Company, Deng Chengjun, appeared in court. The case has now been concluded.

Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company's appeal requests: (1) To revoke the first-instance judgment in accordance with law, and amend the judgment to find that the tower foundation (N4065) of the Xiluodu Right Bank Power Station to Guangdong ±500kV Same-Tower Double-Circuit DC Transmission Line Project owned by Southern Power Grid Company and Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company overlays 231,600 tons of anthracite coal resources within the exploration right area of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company, and order compensation to Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company for losses calculated according to market value, with the specific amount of compensation to be determined by appraisal; (2) To order Southern Power Grid Company and Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company to bear the first-instance and second-instance litigation costs. Facts and reasons: (1) During the construction of the transmission line, Southern Power Grid Company and Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company privately changed the route without fulfilling the obligation to report for approval of overlay of important mineral resources under the "Notice of the Ministry of Land and Resources on Further Improving the Approval and Management of Overlay of Important Mineral Resources by Construction Projects" (Guo Tu Zi Fa [2010] No. 137, hereinafter "Document 137"), and did not negotiate compensation matters with Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company, thus should bear tort liability. Document (2019) No. 584 issued by the Department of Natural Resources of Guizhou Province proves that the currently archived construction route is still the original design route provided by Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company, fully confirming the fact that Southern Power Grid Company and Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company failed to fulfill the reporting obligation. (2) Southern Power Grid Company and Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company should compensate Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company for losses according to market value. First, the value of an exploration right cannot be limited to the input of the exploration right holder. The infringement of an exploration right is an infringement of a usufructuary right as a civil right and interest. For the liability for damages of a usufructuary right, it should be determined based on the property value of such usufructuary right. Second, Article 6 of the "Mineral Resources Law of the People's Republic of China" (hereinafter "Mineral Resources Law") provides that the exploration right holder has a priority right to obtain the mining right for mineral resources within the exploration area. If the exploration right holder can obtain the mining right preferentially, then the property value of the exploration right should obviously converge with the property value of the mining right. Finally, the appraisal opinion confirms that the amount of overlaid resources is 231,600 tons, which Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company cannot exploit or utilize at all, and the overlay has caused huge economic losses. Pursuant to Article 19 of the "Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China" (hereinafter "Tort Liability Law"), "Where property of another person is infringed, property losses shall be calculated according to the market price at the time of loss or by other methods," the economic losses of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company should be calculated according to the market price of coal at the time of damage. The first-instance judgment's finding that Southern Power Grid Company and Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company bear liability for compensation constitutes an error in applying the law.

Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company argued: (1) The first-instance judgment correctly found that Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company did not constitute infringement. The transmission line in question has significant public interest characteristics; the route adjustment was to cooperate with the construction of Bijie Feixiong Airport and had been approved and filed by various levels of government; failure to re-submit for overlay approval was not the fault of Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company. (2) Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company's claim for damages cannot be sustained. First, Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company had no subjective fault for infringement, and the route adjustment itself did not constitute an infringing act. Second, for an exploration right, whether it can be converted into a mining right is subject to significant uncertainty. Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company requests that Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company's appeal be dismissed.

Southern Power Grid Company agreed with the defense opinion of Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company.

Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company's appeal requests: (1) To amend the judgment in accordance with law to dismiss all of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company's claims, and order Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company to bear all first-instance appraisal fees. (2) To amend the judgment to order Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company to bear all litigation costs of the first instance and this appeal. Facts and reasons: (1) The fact of overlay is not established. 1. The estimated surface deformation calculated in the "Appraisal Opinion of the 117 Geological Brigade of the Guizhou Bureau of Geology and Mineral Exploration and Development" (hereinafter "Final Appraisal Opinion") is based on the premise of full extraction of the coal seam, yielding a theoretical maximum surface deformation value. However, in actual mining, it is difficult to achieve full extraction of the coal seam. The transmission tower has strong deformation resistance and is equipped with flexibly adjustable anchor bolts to ensure timely adjustment of the tower. Combined with daily monitoring and inspection measures, in accordance with Articles 21, 22, 42, and 43 of the "Code for Retention of Coal Pillars and Pressure Mining of Buildings, Water Bodies, Railways and Main Shafts," the safety of the N4065 tower foundation can be fully ensured. 2. The "Appraisal Opinion of the 117 Geological Brigade of the Guizhou Bureau of Geology and Mineral Exploration and Development" (the opinion does not bear a seal at the end, was submitted to the first-instance court as a draft for comment, hereinafter "Draft Appraisal Opinion") used the "safe depth calculation method" to conclude that no overlay occurred. During the first-instance trial, the 117 Geological Brigade admitted in court that the "safe depth calculation method" remains an effective appraisal method for determining whether surface buildings or structures overlay coal mines. 3. According to the calculations in the Draft Appraisal Opinion, the mining depth-to-thickness ratios for coal seams C6-1 and C7 below the transmission line both exceed the requirements of the "Code for Design of Overhead Transmission Lines in Mining Affected Areas," satisfying the requirements for foundation stability evaluation of the transmission tower. (2) The compensation for mineral resource losses ordered by the first-instance judgment should be reduced. The calculation method for the compensation amount by the first-instance court can be summarized as: exploration right price paid by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company (RMB 170,246,700) / total resources × overlaid resources = RMB 522,117.6. Given that Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company only paid RMB 102,246,700 of the RMB 170,246,700 exploration right price, and at the conclusion of the first instance, Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company still had not paid the remaining RMB 68,000,000. Therefore, the compensation amount for the resources overlaid by the N4065 tower foundation should be RMB 522,100 × RMB 102,246,700 / RMB 170,246,700 = RMB 313,600.

Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company argued: The appraisal opinion issued by the 117 Geological Brigade should be adopted as the basis for finding that the N4065 tower foundation of Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company overlays the Wangjiaba Coal Mine. The appraisal institution possesses the required qualifications, the selection procedure was lawful, and the appraisal materials were subject to cross-examination by both parties, so it should be accepted by the court. The first-instance court correctly found the actual input costs of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company, and Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company should compensate Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company for interest losses from the date of overlay. Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company requests that Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company's appeal be dismissed.

Southern Power Grid Company agreed with the appeal opinion of Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company.

Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company filed a lawsuit with the first-instance court, requesting: (1) To order Southern Power Grid Company and Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company to jointly compensate Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company for exploration right resource losses and interest losses, provisionally calculated at RMB 181,820,000 (the specific amount of resource losses to be determined by appraisal); (2) To order Southern Power Grid Company and Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company to bear the litigation costs of this case.

The first-instance court found the following facts:

(I) Acquisition of the exploration right for the Wangjiaba Coal Mine and Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company's investment in the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right

1. The original right holder of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right was Yankuang Guizhou Energy and Chemical Co., Ltd. The initial validity period was from December 2, 2003, to July 31, 2006; the first renewal period extended to August 1, 2008; the second renewal period to August 1, 2010; and the third renewal period to August 1, 2012. On August 8, 2011, Yankuang Guizhou Energy and Chemical Co., Ltd. transferred the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right to Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company for RMB 56,100,000. The transfer contract was approved on September 13, 2012. After acquiring the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right, Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company applied for the fourth to seventh renewals, which expired on August 2, 2020. Further investigation shows: The mineral resources exploration license for the Wangjiaba Coal Mine recorded an exploration area of 66.41 square kilometers as of July 27, 2010, with a validity period from July 27, 2010, to August 1, 2012; as of May 28, 2012, an exploration area of 66.53 square kilometers, with a validity period from May 21, 2012, to August 1, 2012; and as of February 15, 2019, an exploration area of 48.08 square kilometers, with a validity period from August 2, 2018, to August 2, 2020.

2. On April 30, 2015, the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province issued the "Notice on Delineating the Mining Area Scope of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine in Xiaoba Town, Bijie Economic Development Zone" (hereinafter "Notice on Delineating Mining Area Scope"), which recorded a mining area of 38.4451 square kilometers, an approved and filed coal resource reserve of 153,520,000 tons, and a planned production capacity of 900,000 tons per year. On April 25, 2017, the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province issued a "Reply to the Report on Applying for Continued Retention of the Mining Area Delineation of Guizhou Huading Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. Wangjiaba Coal Mine," stating: In principle, the reservation period for the delineated mining area of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company is extended for 2 years, after which no further extension will be granted, and disposal should proceed as soon as possible in the merger and reorganization.

3. To determine the exploration right price payable by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company for the resource amount, on commission by the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province, Sichuan Tiandiyuan Land and Resources Real Estate Appraisal Co., Ltd. appraised the exploration right of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine. On February 10, 2012, Sichuan Tiandiyuan Land and Resources Real Estate Appraisal Co., Ltd. issued the "Appraisal Report on the Exploration Right of the Wangjiaba Mine Field Coal Mine in Bijie City, Guizhou Province" (Sichuan Tiandiyuan [2011] (Mine Appraisal) No. 311). Page 1 states: The appraisal base date is July 30, 2011, and the mining area is 66.41 square kilometers. Pages 17-18 state: According to the "Simulated Development and Utilization Plan," the measured internal economic resources (331) of 21,540,000 tons and the controlled internal economic resources (332) of 8,980,000 tons are all designed for utilization; inferred internal economic resources (333) of 41,190,000 tons are converted using a credibility coefficient of 0.8; predicted resources (334)? are not included in the appraisal calculation. After calculation, the resource reserves utilized in this appraisal are 63,472,000 tons, with recoverable reserves of 47,148,100 tons. Pages 29-30 state: Through on-site investigation and analysis of the local market by appraisers, in accordance with the principles and procedures of exploration right appraisal, appropriate appraisal methods and parameters were selected. After careful calculation, the value of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right (appraisal calculation period 32.67 years, including a construction period of 2.67 years and a mine service life of 30 years; the retained reserves proposed to be utilized during the appraisal period are 56,057,800 tons; the recoverable reserves proposed to be utilized during the appraisal period are 37,800,000 tons) at the appraisal base date is RMB 170,246,700. The value per ton of retained reserves proposed to be utilized during the appraisal period is RMB 3.04, and per ton of recoverable reserves proposed to be utilized is RMB 4.5.

4. On April 25, 2012, the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province issued a notice to Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company regarding the payment of the exploration right price. The notice stated that Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company should pay an exploration right price of RMB 170,246,700 for the Wangjiaba Coal Mine, with an initial payment of RMB 102,246,700 due before December 30, 2012, and a second installment of RMB 68,000,000 due before December 30, 2013. At the time of this lawsuit, Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company still owed RMB 68,000,000 of the exploration right price.

5. During the trial, upon inquiry by the court, Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company stated that its investment in the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right was: Purchase price RMB 56,100,000 and the exploration right price paid to the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province of RMB 170,246,700. After Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company acquired the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right on September 13, 2012, upon approval, no new exploration investment was made in the Wangjiaba Coal Mine. At the time Wangjiaba Coal Industry Company acquired the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right, the exploration area was 66.53 square kilometers.

(II) Approval and construction of the transmission project in question

1. On March 31, 2008, the National Development and Reform Commission issued the "Notice of the General Office of the National Development and Reform Commission on China Southern Power Grid Co., Ltd. Carrying Out Preliminary Work for the Xiluodu Right Bank Power Station to Guangdong and Nuozhadu Hydropower Station to Guangdong UHV DC Transmission Projects," stating: To enhance the capacity of the Southern Power Grid's West-East Electricity Transmission Project, to facilitate the power transmission needs of the Nuozhadu Hydropower Station and the Xiluodu Right Bank Power Station, and to meet the electricity demand for the economic and social development of Guangdong Province, preliminary work for the two UHV DC transmission projects, Xiluodu Right Bank Power Station to Guangdong and Nuozhadu Hydropower Station to Guangdong, is approved. Pre-preliminary design review was completed in August 2010. In February 2009, Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company completed the feasibility study for the transmission line of the project in question and reported the situation of overlaid mines to the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province for approval. On November 2, 2009, the Guizhou Provincial Land and Resources Survey and Planning Institute issued the "Review Opinion on the 'Appraisal Report on Mineral Resources Overlay by Construction Land Use for the Xiluodu Right Bank Power Station to Guangdong ±500kV Same-Tower Double-Circuit DC Transmission Project (Banposhan to Shaoji'ao Section),'" stating: The transmission project in question overlaps with the mining area; the underlying coal seam has a large burial depth; no resource amount was estimated; no overlay exists. On December 2, 2009, the former Department of Land and Resources of Guizhou Province issued the "Reply Opinion on the Appraisal of Mineral Resources Overlay by Construction Land Use for the Xiluodu Right Bank Power Station to Guangdong ±500kV Same-Tower Double-Circuit DC Transmission Project (Banshanshan to Shaoji'ao Section)" (hereinafter "Reply Opinion"), which did not record any overlay of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right by the transmission project in question. Meanwhile, on November 5, 2009, the design institute engaged by Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company, China Power Engineering Consulting Group Southwest Electric Power Design Institute, issued a "Letter on Collecting Information and Reporting the Route of the Xiluodu Right Bank Power Station to Guangdong ±500kV Same-Tower Double-Circuit DC Transmission Project" to 26 county and district governments and state-owned assets supervision and administration commissions, development and reform commissions, urban and rural construction planning, land, mineral resources, forestry, transportation, communications, meteorology, water conservancy, cultural relics, seismology, environmental protection, airport authorities, and military units along the route in Yunnan and Guizhou provinces, attaching a route map to solicit opinions. The units gradually affixed their seals to the letter around December 2009, agreeing to the route. At this time, the feasibility study route of the transmission line in question had been determined.

2. On July 21, 2009, the State Council and the Central Military Commission approved the立项 construction of Bijie Feixiong Airport. In October 2009, the Bijie City Planning Bureau issued the Overall Urban Plan of Bijie City (2009-2030), replacing the previous version (2006-2020, last amended in 2008). Article 30 of the plan stipulated: "Make technical preparations for the construction of Bijie Airport, actively create conditions, and strive to start the construction of Bijie Airport in the near future." To coordinate with the construction of Bijie Feixiong Airport and obtain planning and construction permits for the line corridor, CSG EHV Company adjusted the feasibility study route, shifting it northward (preliminary design route and subsequent construction route), to avoid the new Overall Urban Plan of Bijie City and the flight control area of Bijie Feixiong Airport. On March 4, 2011, the design institute hired by CSG EHV Company, Southwest Electric Power Design Institute of China Power Engineering Consulting Group, again issued to the governments of 26 counties and districts in Yunnan and Guizhou provinces along the route of the transmission line project, as well as to the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission, Development and Reform Commission, urban and rural construction planning, land and resources, mineral resources, forestry, transportation, communications, meteorology, water conservancy, cultural relics, earthquake, environmental protection, airport authorities, and military units along the route, the "Letter Regarding the Request for Opinions on the Route Approval of the ±500kV Same-Tower Double-Circuit DC Transmission Line Project from the Right Bank of Xiluodu Hydropower Station to Guangdong," along with the "Line Route Map" and "Tower Location Coordinates," to solicit opinions from entities along the route of the transmission line project. On May 30, 2011, the Bijie City Planning Bureau signed off on the report, agreeing in principle to the route plan and affixed its seal. Meanwhile, CSG EHV Company submitted to the Bijie City Planning Bureau and the Bijie Municipal People's Government the drawings of the preliminary design route formed after shifting northward to avoid the new city plan of Bijie and the area of Bijie Feixiong Airport, and obtained approval on June 18, 2011.

3. In February 2011, the National Development and Reform Commission issued the "Approval of the National Development and Reform Commission on the Construction of the Double-Circuit ±500kV DC Transmission Line Project from the Right Bank of Xiluodu Hydropower Station to Guangdong," approving the commencement of construction of the transmission line project. On July 29, 2011, Guizhou Electric Power Design and Research Institute submitted to the former Guizhou Provincial Department of Land and Resources the "Reply Regarding the Letter on Issues Related to the ±500kV Same-Tower Double-Circuit DC Transmission Line Project from the Right Bank of Xiluodu Hydropower Station to Guangdong," providing the coordinates of each tower foundation of the transmission line project passing through Guizhou Province to the former Guizhou Provincial Department of Land and Resources, which acknowledged receipt on the same day (received by Wu Yueping, who served as Director of the General Office of the former Guizhou Provincial Department of Land and Resources from September 2010 to November 2014). From May 2012 to May 2013, the construction of the transmission line project was completed within the Wangjiaba Coal Mine area. On August 8, 2013, the 16 tower foundations of the transmission line project within the Wangjiaba Coal Mine area were accepted. The transmission line project traverses the Wangjiaba Coal Mine for 7.86 kilometers.

4. In March 2010, commissioned by CSG EHV Company, the 102 Geological Brigade of the Guizhou Provincial Bureau of Geology and Mineral Resources (hereinafter referred to as the 102 Geological Brigade) produced the "Assessment Report on the Mineral Resources Overlain by the Construction Land of the ±500kV Same-Tower Double-Circuit DC Transmission Line Project from the Right Bank of Xiluodu to Guangdong (from Banshan to Shaoji'ao Section)," which indicated the work commencement and completion dates: from June 2, 2009, to July 20, 2009. Page 27, regarding the explanation of the exploration rights along the line, stated: "The proposed transmission line construction project passes through the southwestern part of this mining area, from south-northwest-east in section G13-G14 and from north-west-southeast in section G14-G16, overlapping with the mining area. The overlapping area is the third section of the Yongshen Town Formation of the Lower Triassic System. The underlying coal seams are deeply buried, and no resource estimation has been made. No treatment for overlaying is carried out."

(3) Subsequent Handling After the Overlay

To resolve the insurance compensation issues regarding the overlay of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine, in March 2015, commissioned by CSG EHV Company, the 102 Geological Brigade produced the "Assessment Report on the Mineral Resources of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine in Bijie City, Guizhou Province, Overlain by the DC Line Tower Construction Land of the ±500kV Same-Tower Double-Circuit DC Transmission Line Project from the Right Bank of Xiluodu Hydropower Station to Guangdong" (hereinafter referred to as the 2015 Report). Page 14 stated: "The Wangjiaba Coal Mine in Bijie City has four minable coal seams, using a coal seam group safety coefficient value of 200." Page 15 stated: "There are 2 minable coal seams (C6-1, C7) within the mining area; 2 locally minable coal seams (C6-2, C13)." Page 16 stated: "All locations within the mining area where the tower foundations of the construction project are located are unminable; the safe depth is 646 meters." Page 17 stated: "The construction land for the tower foundations of the DC line of the ±500kV Same-Tower Double-Circuit DC Transmission Line Project from the Right Bank of Xiluodu Hydropower Station to Guangdong overlays 224 tons of anthracite coal resources (exploration right) of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine in Bijie City [including (332) resources of 68 tons, (333) resources of 66 tons, (334)? resources of 90 tons]." Wangjiaba Coal Industry used this evidence to prove that the transmission line project constructed by CSG EHV Company overlayed their exploration rights, but did not accept the amount of overlain resources. CSG EHV Company did not accept the conclusion regarding the overlay stated in the report.

(4) Trial at First Instance

1. Wangjiaba Coal Industry did not provide evidence within the time required by the court to prove its exploration investment within the scope of the transmission line project's overlay of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration rights. After repeated inquiries by the court, Wangjiaba Coal Industry claimed that its loss was RMB 181.82 million for the loss of exploration right resources (mineral resources) and did not claim losses for exploration investment. The calculation standard was: total overlain resources of 17.218 million tons, calculated at RMB 220 per ton, multiplied by 20%.

2. In September 2018, commissioned by CSG EHV Company, the 102 Geological Brigade produced the "Assessment Report on the Mineral Resources of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine in Bijie City, Guizhou Province, Overlain by the DC Line Tower Construction Land of the ±500kV Same-Tower Double-Circuit DC Transmission Line Project from the Right Bank of Xiluodu Hydropower Station to Guangdong" (hereinafter referred to as the 2018 Report). Page 15 stated: "There are 2 minable coal seams (C6-1, C7) within the mining area; 2 locally minable coal seams (C6-2, C13)." Page 16 stated: "The locations of the tower foundations of the construction project within the mining area for the C6-2 and C13 coal seams are all unminable; the safe depth is 348 meters." Page 17 stated: "The minable coal seams (C6-1 and C7) beneath the 16 tower foundations of the construction project are deeply buried, and the bottom elevation of the coal seams is below the elevation corresponding to the safe depth (348 meters). Therefore, the 16 tower foundations located within the scope of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine mining area did not overlay any coal resources of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine. Evaluation cut-off date: September 13, 2018."

3. On September 19, 2018, the 102 Geological Brigade issued the "Explanation on the Calculation Standards of the 'Assessment Report on the Mineral Resources of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine in Bijie City, Guizhou Province, Overlain by the DC Line Tower Construction Land of the ±500kV Same-Tower Double-Circuit DC Transmission Line Project from the Right Bank of Xiluodu Hydropower Station to Guangdong,'" stating: "In the 'Assessment Report' compiled in March 2015, it was considered that the mining area was an exploration right area. From a safety perspective, to prevent over-exploitation of the mining area, the safety coefficient was raised to a higher grade, and the corresponding safety coefficient was taken as 200. Based on the actual protection grade requirements determined by the 'Code for Pillar Retention and Coal Mining under Buildings, Water Bodies, Railways, and Main Shafts and Tunnels' and the 'Safety Stability Analysis Report of Tower Positions Crossing the Wangjiaba Coal Mine Exploration Right Area' compiled by Southwest Electric Power Design Institute, and also based on the expert opinions in the 'Minutes of the Seminar on the Overlay of Mineral Resources by the ±500kV Same-Tower Double-Circuit DC Transmission Line Project from the Right Bank of Xiluodu Hydropower Station to Guangdong Crossing the Bijie Wangjiaba Coal Mine' (September 5, 2018), the safety coefficient was revised. Therefore, in the 'Assessment Report' compiled in September 2018, the safety coefficient corresponding to the protection grade was taken as 150. Consequently, due to the changes in these calculation parameters, the safe depth in the 'Assessment Report' compiled in September 2018 is 348 meters. The overlay scope was determined based on the protection grade of the construction project, protective belt, movement angle, safe depth, etc. After comprehensive analysis through mapping, the 16 tower foundation lands of the Xiluodu DC line construction project did not overlay any mineral resources of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine in Bijie City, Guizhou Province." Upon application by CSG EHV Company, the 102 Geological Brigade dispatched its staff member Ban Guohua to appear in court for questioning by the court and cross-examination by both parties.

4. Commissioned by Wangjiaba Coal Industry, the Nanjing Design and Research Institute of China Coal Technology and Engineering Group produced in September 2017 the "Design Instruction for Protective Coal Pillars of ±500kV Transmission Line Tower Foundations in the Wangjiaba Mine Field of Bijie City, Guizhou Province." Page 21 stated: "Within the scope of the overlay area of the ±500kV transmission line tower foundations in the Wangjiaba mine field, the C6-2 and C13 coal seams are both unminable. The tower foundations mainly overlay the C6-1 and C7 coal resources of the mine field. The total overlain resource is 17.218 million tons, including 1.47 million tons of controlled resources (332), 3.298 million tons of inferred resources (333), and 12.45 million tons of predicted resources (334)?" CSG and CSG EHV Company did not accept this result. Commissioned by CSG EHV Company, Tiandi Science and Technology Co., Ltd. issued in December 2018 the "Calculation of Protective Coal Pillar Quantity for the ±500kV Same-Tower Double-Circuit DC Transmission Line Project from the Right Bank of Xiluodu Hydropower Station to Guangdong Crossing the Wangjiaba Mine Field," page 53 stating: "Based on the cross-reference relationship between the minable coal seam range obtained from the reconnaissance and exploration of the Wangjiaba mine field and the aboveground and underground positions of the transmission line towers, the C6-2 and C13 coal seams below and around the transmission line are unminable due to their occurrence conditions. The coal seams requiring the delineation of protective coal pillars are C6-1 and C7. The protective coal pillars for the high-voltage transmission line need to be delineated as independent protective coal pillars for each tower... Using the geological block method, the resource amounts of the protective coal pillars for the towers were calculated. For the 15 tower foundations, the total resource of C6-1 coal seam protective coal pillars is 8.467 million tons, and for C7 coal seam protective coal pillars is 5.1 million tons, totaling 13.567 million tons. Among these, (332) resources are 1.32 million tons, (333) resources are 2.133 million tons, and (334)? resources are 10.114 million tons."

5.
