The first-instance court found that the issues in dispute were: (1) whether Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. had standing as a plaintiff; (2) whether the transmission project constituted pressing of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right; (3) what the legal relationship was and the amount of compensation (damages) to be awarded to Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd.; (4) whether China Southern Power Grid Co., Ltd. bore liability.

(1) Whether Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. had standing as a plaintiff

First, an exploration right is both a usufructuary right and bears the legal characteristics of an administrative license. Therefore, Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd.'s exploration right for the Wangjiaba Coal Mine was established on the effective date of the administrative license decision. Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. obtained a new Mineral Resources Exploration Permit for the Wangjiaba Coal Mine (valid from August 2, 2018 to August 2, 2020) on February 15, 2019, following the renewal of the exploration right. This permit was the result of the administrative authority responsible for mineral resources management approving the renewal of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right. Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. had obtained approval for the renewal of the exploration right and thus acquired standing as a plaintiff. Whether the administrative authority's act of renewing the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right seven times without Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. having fully paid the exploration right resource price constituted an illegal approval was beyond the scope of civil litigation. If China Southern Power Grid Co., Ltd. and China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. disputed this, they could raise it with the relevant administrative authority or initiate a separate action. Their defense that Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. obtained the renewal of the exploration right illegally and therefore lacked standing was not sustainable, and the first-instance court did not accept it.

Second, Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. acquired the exploration right to the Wangjiaba Coal Mine on September 13, 2012, after the transfer was approved, and thus had standing as the holder of the exploration right. Although construction of the transmission project within the Wangjiaba Coal Mine area commenced in May 2012, it was not completed until May 2013. Since the construction continued after Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. became the holder of the exploration right, Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. had the right to assert claims against China Southern Power Grid Co., Ltd. and China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. Moreover, Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. acquired the exploration right from Yankuang Guizhou Energy Co., Ltd., thereby obtaining standing as the holder of the exploration right. There was no pending lawsuit at the time of the transfer, and the subject of the transaction was not a right of action. Therefore, the defense of China Southern Power Grid Co., Ltd. and China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. that the right of action belonged to Yankuang Guizhou Energy Co., Ltd. and that the right of action could not be transferred was not sustainable, and the first-instance court did not accept it.

Third, China Southern Power Grid Co., Ltd. and China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. argued that since the mineral resources were owned by the state, Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. had no legal basis to claim compensation for "resource losses" and lacked standing as a plaintiff. The first-instance court held that this defense pertained to whether Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd.'s claims could be supported, not to whether it had standing as a plaintiff. Moreover, although Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. was not the owner of the mineral resources of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine, its exploration right over the mine was a usufructuary right protected by law. The value of that right was related to the quantity of mineral resources. Therefore, it was not improper for Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. to seek compensation for losses of exploration right resources. Furthermore, interpreting Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd.'s claims did not lead to the conclusion that it was asserting ownership of the mineral resources. Thus, the defense of China Southern Power Grid Co., Ltd. and China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. that Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. lacked standing because it claimed ownership of the mineral resources was not accepted by the first-instance court.

In summary, Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. currently held the Mineral Resources Exploration Permit for the Wangjiaba Coal Mine and was the holder of the exploration right, making it a proper plaintiff in this case.

(2) Whether the transmission project constituted pressing of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right

Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. relied on the 2015 Report to argue that the transmission project constituted pressing of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right. China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. relied on the 2018 Report and its calculation notes, as well as appraisal reports issued by Tiandi Science and Technology Co., Ltd. and Southwest Electric Power Design Institute Co., Ltd., to argue that it did not constitute pressing. The first-instance court found that the same personnel from the 102 Geological Brigade had issued contradictory appraisal reports for the same subject matter. Although the 102 Geological Brigade sent relevant personnel to appear in court for cross-examination and issued a written explanation, the explanation was not accepted by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd., was rather strained, and lacked credibility. Tiandi Science and Technology Co., Ltd. and Southwest Electric Power Design Institute Co., Ltd. had appraisal qualifications, but they were selected unilaterally by China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. after the case was filed, and their neutrality was challenged by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. Given that Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. did not accept the appraisal conclusions of those two entities, its application for the first-instance court to appoint a neutral third party to conduct an investigation and appraisal of the pressing scope and quantity of pressed resources of the transmission project should be granted. Upon the joint selection of both Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. and China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd., the first-instance court appointed the 117 Geological Brigade to conduct a judicial appraisal. In the "Draft Appraisal Opinion," the 117 Geological Brigade used two methods. The first method was the same "safe depth method" used in the 2018 Report, and the conclusion was consistent: no pressing. However, the second method, the "surface deformation method," led to the conclusion that tower foundation N4065 of the transmission project pressed 231,600 tons of coal resource quantity in the C7 coal seam of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine. The appraisal unit, at the request of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd., removed the appraisal opinion based on the "safe depth method" and retained only the conclusion based on the "surface deformation method." Therefore, the transmission project already constituted pressing of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right. The defense of China Southern Power Grid Co., Ltd. and China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. that the transmission project did not constitute pressing was not sustainable, and the first-instance court did not accept it.

(3) The legal relationship and the amount of compensation (damages) payable to Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd.

1. Pursuant to Article 123 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter "Property Law"), which provides that "the right to explore and the right to mine, the right to use water, and the right to use water surfaces and tidal flats for aquaculture and fishing, lawfully obtained, shall be protected by law," the exploration right lawfully obtained by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. was protected by law. Pursuant to Article 6, Paragraph 1 of the Tort Liability Law, which provides that "one who through fault infringes upon a civil right or interest of another person shall bear tort liability," Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd., in claiming that China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. committed a tort, had to prove that China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. was at fault in carrying out the act of pressing mineral resources. Based on the facts found, the transmission project was approved by the National Development and Reform Commission in 2008 to implement the national strategy of "transmitting electricity from the west to the east" and was inherently for public benefit. As early as before Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. acquired the exploration right (transferred on August 8, 2011, approved on September 13, 2012), the former Guizhou Provincial Department of Land and Resources issued a "Reply" on December 2, 2009, approving the pressing of mineral resources by related mines for the construction of the transmission project. At that time, the feasibility study route for the transmission line of the project had already been determined. Due to the construction of Bijie Feixiong Airport, the urban planning of Bijie City was adjusted, requiring the originally approved feasibility study route to be shifted 2 kilometers north to obtain approval from the Bijie Municipal People's Government. After modifying the construction route, Guizhou Electric Power Design Institute submitted to the former Guizhou Provincial Department of Land and Resources the coordinates of each tower foundation of the transmission project passing through Guizhou Province. The former Guizhou Provincial Department of Land and Resources did not raise any objection upon receipt, nor did it raise any opinion regarding the construction activities of China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. during or after the construction of the transmission project. Therefore, there was no subjective fault on the part of China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. in shifting the feasibility study route of the transmission project 2 kilometers north for construction, and no tort was constituted. The defense of China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. that it lacked fault for tort was valid, and the first-instance court accepted it.

In summary, the claim by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. that China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. committed a tort was inconsistent with the facts found by the first-instance court and was not accepted. The transmission project constructed by China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. was for the public interest. The pressing of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd.'s mine entitled Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. to compensation in accordance with Article 123 of the Property Law and other provisions. This case was properly characterized as a dispute over the protection of property rights.

2. According to the conclusions of the Final Appraisal Opinion and the testimony of the appraisal personnel during court appearance, tower foundation N4065 pressed 231,600 tons of Wangjiaba Coal Mine resources. Because Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. was unable to submit a "Mining Utilization Plan" and "Safety Evaluation Plan" approved by the relevant administrative authority, the appraisal unit appointed by the first-instance court, lacking qualifications for coal mining design and safety evaluation, could not determine whether the 12,385,100 tons of resource quantity for protective coal pillars under the remaining 15 tower foundations could be developed and utilized. This would require further demonstration by an institution with coal mining design and safety evaluation qualifications. Although the appraisal unit concluded that "the 12,385,100 tons may not be treated as pressed," Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd.'s exploration right would ultimately need to be converted into a mining right to realize its value, and recovering costs through mining would require consideration of whether the resources could be developed and utilized. If the mineral resources could not be developed and utilized, this would become a loss for Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. Therefore, this case required further evaluation and appraisal of whether the 12,385,100 tons of resource quantity for protective coal pillars under the remaining 15 tower foundations could be developed and utilized. Given that Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. stated in court that "compensation for the approximately 12.38 million tons of resources pressed by the 15 tower foundations is not sought in this case and will be pursued in a separate action when conditions are ripe," and subsequently submitted a "Motion to Amend the Statement of Claims" withdrawing the claim for compensation for the 12,385,100 tons of resource quantity for protective coal pillars under the 15 tower foundations, the application of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. complied with legal provisions. The first-instance court granted the application and did not address that part of the claim in this case. Therefore, the resource quantity of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right pressed by the transmission project was 231,600 tons, comprising: (332) resource quantity: 134,500 tons; (333) resource quantity: 75,400 tons; and (334)? resource quantity: 21,700 tons.

The first-instance court held that mineral resources are owned by the state, and mining right holders only have usufructuary rights. The pressing act in this case arose from a project implemented to carry out the national strategy of "transmitting electricity from the west to the east," which had a significant public interest character. As discussed above, Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd.'s claim that China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. committed a tort was not established. However, the transmission line constructed by China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. did press a portion of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd.'s mine, and China Southern Power Grid EHV Transmission Co., Ltd. was legally obliged to compensate for the losses caused thereby. Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. held the exploration right for the Wangjiaba Coal Mine. For an exploration right, the possibility of converting it into a mining right was uncertain. Even if the exploration right was converted into a mining right, the holder of the exploration right would still need to pay necessary usage fees to the state for the realization of the mining right and invest substantial construction and production operation costs. From a market risk perspective, investment in a mining right also faced the risk of fluctuations in the market price of mineral products, and the expected profit of the mining right holder might not be realized. Therefore, the compensation to be received by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. should be limited to the amount of the price payable for the pressed resource reserves under current market conditions, as well as direct losses such as the exploration investment allocated to the pressed mining area, investment in existing mining facilities, and costs for relocating corresponding facilities. In the absence of claims by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. for direct losses such as the exploration investment allocated to the pressed mining area, investment in existing mining facilities, and costs for relocating corresponding facilities, compensation was to be based on the amount payable for the pressed resource reserves under current market conditions, plus compensation for the loss of exploration right investment allocated to the pressed mining area. Adopting the principle of making whole, compensating the mining right holder for actual losses caused by the pressing of mineral resources was fair and reasonable and balanced with the value orientation of achieving public interest. Therefore, the application of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. for appraisal and evaluation of the market value of the pressed mineral resource quantity and the achievable profit amount was not granted.

In this case, to determine the exploration right price that Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. should pay for the resource quantity, upon entrustment by the former Guizhou Provincial Department of Land and Resources, Sichuan Tiandiyuan Land and Resources Real Estate Appraisal Co., Ltd. evaluated the exploration right of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine. The appraisal conclusion was: "According to the 'Simulated Development and Utilization Plan,' the measured internal economic resource quantity (331) of 21.54 million tons and the indicated internal economic resource quantity (332) of 8.98 million tons of the mine are fully designed and utilized; the inferred internal economic resource quantity (333) of 41.19 million tons is discounted by a reliability coefficient of 0.8; the predicted resource quantity (334)? is not included in the appraisal calculation. As calculated, the resource reserves utilized in this project are 63.472 million tons. The value as of the appraisal base date (July 30, 2011) is RMB 170,246,700." The former Guizhou Provincial Department of Land and Resources, based on the above appraisal opinion, issued a notice to Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. requiring payment of an exploration right price of RMB 170,246,700. Therefore, the calculation method for the resource quantity price paid by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. to the relevant state authority was: the measured internal economic resource quantity (331) and the indicated internal economic resource quantity (332) were fully designed and utilized; the inferred internal economic resource quantity (333) was discounted by a reliability coefficient of 0.8; the predicted resource quantity (334)? was not included in the appraisal calculation. The calculation yields (331) + (332) + (333) x 0.8 = 63.472 million tons. The price per ton paid by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. was RMB 170,246,700 ÷ 63.472 million tons = RMB 2.68 per ton.

The former Guizhou Provincial Department of Land and Resources, based on the above appraisal opinion, issued a notice to Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. requiring payment of RMB 170,246,700 for the exploration right premium. Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. had already paid RMB 102,246,700 in accordance with the notice. Although as of the time of this litigation Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. still owed RMB 68,000,000 for the exploration right premium, Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. was not discontinuing payment. Therefore, the defense of China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company that Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. had not fully paid the exploration right premium and thus it refused to pay the compensation for the overlaid resource volume could not be established. The compensation for the overlaid resource volume was calculated as (331) + (332) + (333) x 0.8 for the overlaid resource volume, with the resource volume price calculated at RMB 2.68 per ton. In summary, the compensation that Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. should receive is calculated as follows: (1) Compensation for the overlaid resource volume: Given that tower foundation (N4065) overlays 231,600 tons of anthracite coal resource volume of coal seam C7, including (332) resource volume of 134,500 tons; (333) resource volume of 75,400 tons; (334)? resource volume of 21,700 tons. Therefore, [(331) + (332) + (333) x 0.8] x RMB 2.68 = 194,820 tons x RMB 2.68 = RMB 522,117.6. (2) Compensation for investment in exploration right and exploration expenses: The Notice on Delineating the Scope of the Mining Zone states that the coal resource volume reviewed and filed is 153,520,000 tons, and the overlaid resource volume is 231,600 tons, accounting for 0.151% of 153,520,000 tons. Given that Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. paid RMB 56,100,000 for the acquisition of the exploration right, and after Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. acquired the exploration right on August 8, 2011, and obtained approval for the transfer on September 13, 2012, no new exploration investment was made in the Wangjiaba Coal Mine. Therefore, the compensation for the exploration right investment is calculated as: RMB 56,100,000 x 0.151% = RMB 84,711. (3) Compensation for mine construction investment: Given that Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. did not submit evidence to prove that it had made construction investment in the Wangjiaba Coal Mine, there is no compensation for this part. The compensation that Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. should receive is RMB 606,828.6, including resource volume compensation of RMB 522,117.6 and exploration right investment compensation of RMB 84,711.

At the same time, China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company should also compensate Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. for the interest on the above investment losses at the loan interest rate of the same period. The interest on the resource volume compensation of RMB 522,117.6 is calculated as follows: from January 1, 2013 to August 19, 2019, based on the benchmark interest rate for loans of the same type and same period published by the People's Bank of China; from August 20, 2019 to the date of actual performance, based on the loan prime rate published by the National Interbank Funding Center. The interest on the exploration right investment compensation of RMB 84,711 is calculated as follows: from August 9, 2011 to August 19, 2019, based on the benchmark interest rate for loans of the same type and same period published by the People's Bank of China; from August 20, 2019 to the date of actual performance, based on the loan prime rate published by the National Interbank Funding Center.

(4) On the issue of whether China Southern Power Grid Corporation should bear responsibility

In accordance with Article 14 of the Company Law of the PRC, which provides that "a branch does not have the status of a legal person, and its civil liability shall be borne by the company," China Southern Power Grid Corporation, as the parent company of China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company, shall bear civil liability in this case according to law.

In summary, the claims of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. were partially established. The judgment of first instance was: (1) China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company shall compensate Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 606,828.6 (including: compensation for overlaid mineral resource volume of RMB 522,117.6; exploration right investment compensation of RMB 84,711) plus interest (the interest on the resource volume compensation of RMB 522,117.6 is calculated as follows: from January 1, 2013 to August 19, 2019, based on the benchmark interest rate for loans of the same type and same period published by the People's Bank of China; from August 20, 2019 to the date of actual performance, based on the loan prime rate published by the National Interbank Funding Center. The interest on the exploration right investment compensation of RMB 84,711 is calculated as follows: from August 9, 2011 to August 19, 2019, based on the benchmark interest rate for loans of the same type and same period published by the People's Bank of China; from August 20, 2019 to the date of actual performance, based on the loan prime rate published by the National Interbank Funding Center). (2) China Southern Power Grid Corporation shall bear supplementary liability for the portion of the debt in this case that China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company is unable to satisfy. (3) The other claims of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. were dismissed. The first instance case acceptance fee of RMB 59,431.25 was borne by China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company in the amount of RMB 9,868.29 and by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 49,562.96. The appraisal fee of RMB 350,000 was borne by China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company in the amount of RMB 21,875 and by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 328,125.

During the second instance of this Court, Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. submitted evidence in accordance with law in support of its appeal claims. This Court organized the parties to exchange evidence and conduct cross-examination. The first piece of evidence was the Report on Verification and Exploration of Resource Reserves prepared by Shandong Taishan Resource Exploration Co., Ltd., which intended to prove that with the further deepening of coal mine exploration, the resource reserves found by the court of first instance had changed, and the overlaid resource volume should be recalculated based on the new exploration report. The second piece of evidence was the Notice on Approving the Change Registration of the Exploration Right (Reservation) of Bijie Wangjiaba Well Field Coal Mine, Guizhou Province (hereinafter referred to as the Change Registration Notice) issued by the Department of Natural Resources of Guizhou Province, which intended to prove that according to the requirements of this notice, all coal seam mineral resources under the N4065 tower foundation had been overlaid, and the judgment of first instance was clearly improper in calculating the overlaid resource volume based only on coal seam C7. China Southern Power Grid Corporation and China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company had no objection to the authenticity of the first piece of evidence, but did not recognize its legality and relevance, and believed that it could not achieve the purpose of proof. They had no objection to the authenticity and legality of the second piece of evidence, but did not recognize its relevance, and believed that it could not achieve the purpose of proof. China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company argued that, according to the Report on Verification and Exploration of Resource Reserves and the Change Registration Notice, it could actually be confirmed that after the change registration of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd.'s exploration right this time, the N4065 tower foundation was no longer within the exploration block area of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine, and thus did not constitute an overlay on the Wangjiaba Coal Mine. This Court determined the authenticity, legality, and relevance of the evidence submitted by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. Whether it could achieve the purpose of proof would be commented on later.

Regarding the facts disputed by the parties, this Court finds as follows: (1) In August 2021, Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. commissioned Shandong Taishan Resource Exploration Co., Ltd. to prepare the Report on Verification and Exploration of Resource Reserves. The report stated that the main geological purpose of this exploration work was to ascertain the coal resource reserves within the Wangjiaba Coal Mine area, to provide geological data basis for the conversion of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine exploration right to a mining right, to apply for a mining license with an annual capacity of 900,000 tons, and for the feasibility study and preliminary design of mine construction. (2) The Department of Natural Resources of Guizhou Province issued the Change Registration Notice in November 2021, which stated: the exploration scope applied for change this time overlaps with the border of the construction project already entered into the database of our department -- the Xiluodu Right Bank Power Transmission to Guangdong +-500kV Same-Tower Double-Circuit DC Transmission Project (from Banshanshan to Shaojiao)... According to the current regulations, when applying for registration of "conversion of exploration right to mining right," the mining right scope should avoid the construction project scope.

This Court is of the opinion that the disputed issues in this second instance are: (1) whether the N4065 tower foundation overlays the Wangjiaba Coal Mine; (2) what liability China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company should bear.

(1) On the issue of whether the N4065 tower foundation overlays the Wangjiaba Coal Mine

During the trial of first instance in this case, upon joint selection by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. and China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company, the court of first instance commissioned No. 117 Geological Brigade to appraise whether 16 tower foundations, including N4065, overlaid the Wangjiaba Coal Mine. No. 117 Geological Brigade issued the Appraisal Opinion (Draft for Comments), and after soliciting opinions from all parties, formed the Final Appraisal Opinion. The Final Appraisal Opinion, using the "surface deformation method," confirmed that the N4065 tower foundation constituted an overlay of 231,600 tons of coal resources in coal seam C7. After the appraiser appeared in court to explain, under the assumption that no protective coal pillars were left for the coal seam, the maximum surface tilt value after mining coal seam C7 was at the subsidence basin of the N4065 tower, with a surface tilt value of 5.04mm/m, which was greater than the maximum allowable value of 5mm/m specified in the standard. China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company acknowledged the Calculation Results Table of Maximum Ground Movement Deformation Values after Mining Coal Seam C6-1 Below Tower Foundations (N4060-N4075) and the Calculation Results Table of Maximum Ground Movement Deformation Values after Mining Coal Seam C7 Below Tower Foundations (N4060-N4075) on which No. 117 Geological Brigade based the above appraisal conclusion. This Court is of the opinion that No. 117 Geological Brigade was jointly selected by both parties and commissioned by the court, and both the appraisal institution and its personnel had the corresponding qualifications. During the appraisal process, the court of first instance organized the parties to cross-examine the appraisal materials, organized the appraisal unit and the parties to jointly collect evidence materials, and went to the inspection site for inspection and measurement; the appraisal procedure was lawful. The appraiser appeared in court in accordance with law to accept questions from both parties, and the appraisal should be adopted. China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company argued that the condition for the Final Appraisal Opinion to determine the existence of overlay was full mining of the coal seam, which is difficult to occur in practice. However, China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company did not submit sufficient evidence to prove this claim, and this Court does not accept it. Regarding the impact that full mining of the coal seam would have on the safety of the tower foundation, the Final Appraisal Opinion conducted a scientific analysis and verification, and its probative force is clearly stronger than the unilateral inference of China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company. The court of first instance was not improper in determining, based on the Final Appraisal Opinion, that the N4065 tower foundation constituted an overlay of coal seam C7.

(2) On the issue of what liability China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company should bear

1. Article 33 of the Mineral Resources Law provides: "Before constructing railways, factories, reservoirs, oil pipelines, power transmission projects, and various large buildings or building complexes, the construction unit must consult with the competent department of geology and mineral resources of the relevant province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government to understand the distribution and mining status of mineral resources in the area where the proposed project is located. Without approval from the department authorized by the State Council, important mineral deposits shall not be overlaid." Document No. 137 provides: "All construction projects that, after implementation, render the identified important mineral resources in the overlaid area unable to be exploited and utilized shall be submitted for approval in accordance with the provisions of this notice." In February 2009, China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company completed the feasibility study for the power transmission line of the transmission project involved in the case and reported to the former Guizhou Provincial Department of Land and Resources for approval of the overlay of mineral resources. Later, to cooperate with the construction of Bijie Feixiong Airport, China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company shifted the feasibility study route northward to avoid the new overall urban planning of Bijie City and the flight control area of Bijie Feixiong Airport, but did not re-submit for approval of the overlay of mineral resources for the adjusted route. This Court is of the opinion that when China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company first submitted for approval of mineral resource overlay, the transmission project involved in the case did not yet overlay the mineral resources of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine. After adjusting the project route, the transmission project involved in the case constituted an overlay of the mineral resources of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine. The legal effect of the original approval could not extend to the new overlay act, and China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company should have re-submitted for approval of the overlay. However, considering the actual circumstances of this case, the adjustment of the project route was based on the legitimate reason of constructing the Bijie Feixiong Airport. The adjusted route had been approved and ratified by the National Development and Reform Commission, and Guizhou Electric Power Design Institute promptly reported the tower foundation coordinates to the former Guizhou Provincial Department of Land and Resources. It can be determined that China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company did not intend to evade the approval of mineral resource overlay. Furthermore, considering the fact that the former Guizhou Provincial Department of Land and Resources did not raise any objections during the project construction, the court of first instance was not improper in determining that China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company did not constitute infringement, and this Court affirms that determination.

2. The transmission project constructed by China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company traversed the mining area of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine. Among them, the construction of the N4065 tower foundation, while using the surface land, objectively affected the mining of the underground coal seam C7, restricting the full exercise of the exploration right of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine. China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company should bear corresponding liability for the losses caused to Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. as a result. On the other hand, the transmission project involved in the case is a public interest infrastructure approved by the National Development and Reform Commission, which is significant for improving the capacity of the West-to-East Power Transmission Project, promoting optimal allocation of resources, and improving the ecological environment. China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company constructed the project in accordance with the approval of the National Development and Reform Commission. If, in accordance with Article 19 of the Tort Liability Law, China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company were to compensate for losses based on the market price of the overlaid mineral resources, it would lack legal basis and be unfair.

This Court is of the opinion that the construction of the transmission project involved in the case caused the exploration right originally belonging to Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. to yield to the public interest safeguarded by the transmission project. Therefore, regarding what liability China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company should bear, the focus should be on balancing public interest and private interests, and compensation should be based on actual investment costs. The court of first instance, by reference to Document No. 137, determined that China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company should compensate for the losses of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. at the standard of "(1) the amount of premium payable by the mining right holder for the overlaid resource reserves under current market conditions (excluding those obtained gratuitously); (2) direct losses such as exploration investments shared by the overlaid mineral resources, investments in established mining facilities, and relocation of corresponding facilities." This appropriately balanced the public interest and the civil rights and interests of China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company and Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd., and should be affirmed.

3. By reference to Document No. 137, this Court evaluates the specific amount of compensation as follows: First, regarding the amount of premium payable for the overlaid resource reserves of the exploration right under current market conditions. It has been ascertained that, to determine the exploration right premium payable by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. for the resource reserves, the former Guizhou Provincial Department of Land and Resources commissioned Sichuan Tiandiyuan Land Resource Real Estate Appraisal Co., Ltd. to evaluate the value of the exploration right of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine. The appraisal conclusion stated: "According to the Simulated Development and Utilization Plan, the measured internal economic resource volume (331) of 21,540,000 tons and the indicated internal economic resource volume (332) of 8,980,000 tons of this mine are all designed for utilization; the inferred internal economic resource volume (333) of 41,190,000 tons is converted using a confidence coefficient of 0.8; the predicted resource volume (334)? does not participate in the evaluation calculation. After calculation, the resource volume utilized in this project evaluation is 63,472,000 tons. The value at the base date of evaluation (July 30, 2011) is RMB 170,246,700." The resource volume for which Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. should calculate the exploration right premium is (331) + (332) + (333) x 0.8 = 63,472,000 tons, and the premium per ton of resource volume is RMB 170,246,700 / 63,472,000 tons = RMB 2.68. Combined with the fact that the N4065 tower foundation overlays the indicated internal economic resource volume (332) of 134,500 tons and the inferred internal economic resource volume (333) of 75,400 tons of coal seam C7, it can be determined that the exploration right premium corresponding to the overlaid resource volume is [(332) + (333) x 0.8] x RMB 2.68 = 194,820 tons x RMB 2.68 = RMB 522,117.6. Second, regarding direct losses such as exploration investments shared by the overlaid mineral resources, investments in established mining facilities, and relocation of corresponding facilities. According to the Final Appraisal Opinion, the overlaid resource reserves of 231,600 tons account for 0.151% of the total resource reserves of 153,520,000 tons. Combined with the fact that Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. invested RMB 56,100,000 in the acquisition of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine and did not make further exploration investments thereafter, the amount of direct losses can be determined as RMB 56,100,000 x 0.151% = RMB 84,711. The judgment of first instance was not improper in determining that China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company should compensate Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 522,117.6 + RMB 84,711 = RMB 606,828.6.

Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. appealed, arguing that, according to the latest exploration results of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine, Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. commissioned Shandong Taishan Resource Exploration Co., Ltd. to prepare the Report on Verification and Exploration of Resource Reserves. This report confirmed that with the further deepening of coal mine exploration, the resource reserves found by the court of first instance had changed, and the overlaid resource volume should be recalculated based on the new exploration report. This Court is of the opinion that, first, mineral resources are concealed and uncertain due to their occurrence state, and must go through scientific estimation of resource volume by geological exploration and be submitted for reserve review and filing. A geological exploration report that has passed review is the basis and prerequisite for the transfer of mining rights, and also the basis for determining the transfer price. It has strong credibility and cannot be changed without statutory procedures. It has been ascertained that in 2015, the former Guizhou Provincial Department of Land and Resources had already issued the Notice on Delineating the Scope of the Mining Zone, determining that the filed coal resource reserves of the Wangjiaba Coal Mine were 153,520,000 tons. The exploration report prepared unilaterally by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. had not undergone re-submission for reserve review and filing, and was insufficient to prove that the reserves had changed. Even if the exploration report could achieve the purpose of proof claimed by Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd., it could not request that China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company compensate for the newly added resource reserves. Article 9 of the Interim Administrative Measures for the Collection of Transfer Income from Mining Rights issued by the Ministry of Finance and the former Ministry of Land and Resources provides that where exploration rights and mining rights add mineral types or increase resource reserves, for the added or increased portion, the transfer income shall be collected by reference to the method of transfer by agreement. This provision indicates that adding mineral types or increasing resource reserves within the mining area should belong to the State, and after discovery, the State transfers them to the mining right holder. The rights that the exploration right holder enjoys over the added mineral types and resource reserves do not begin from the time of establishment of the exploration right. In other words, the property right of China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company over the N4065 tower foundation is a prior right compared to the exploration right of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. over the newly discovered reserves, and has priority in property law. The claim of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. that, based on the reserves discovered after the overlay, the grounds for compensation of the court of first instance were erroneous, cannot be established. Furthermore, this claim of Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. also contradicts its litigation claims and appeal claims that China Southern Power Grid Corporation and China Southern Power Grid Ultra High Voltage Company should compensate for losses based on the standard of 231,600 tons determined by the appraisal conclusion.

Wangjiaba Coal Industry also contended that, pursuant to the requirement in the Notice of Change Registration that Wangjiaba Coal Mine should avoid the scope of the power transmission project construction when applying for conversion from exploration right to mining right, all coal seams in the area overlapping with the N4065 tower foundation had been overlain. The court of first instance only calculated the overlain resource amount based on the C7 coal seam, which was clearly improper. This Court finds that this assertion has also exceeded its claims and grounds of appeal. Moreover, according to the provisions of Document No. 137, if the overlain area of a construction project overlaps with the exploration block or mining area but does not affect normal exploration and mining of mineral resources, it shall not be treated as overlain. Therefore, coal seams that overlap with the N4065 tower foundation but can still be normally mined without being affected by the tower foundation shall not be included in the compensation scope for overlain resources. The Final Draft of Appraisal Opinion adopted the "surface deformation method" and confirmed that the N4065 tower foundation only overlays the C7 coal seam. The content in the Notice of Change Registration that "the mining right scope shall avoid the construction project scope" is a principle provision regarding the delimitation of the mining area for a mining right that may be obtained in the future, and is insufficient to overturn the identification of overlain coal seams in the Final Draft of Appraisal Opinion.

Southern Grid Ultra-high Voltage Company appealed, arguing that according to the Resource Reserve Verification and Exploration Report and the Notice of Change Registration, it could be shown that after the change registration of Wangjiaba Coal Industry's exploration right in this case, the N4065 tower foundation was no longer within the exploration block of Wangjiaba Coal Mine, and thus did not constitute an overlay on Wangjiaba Coal Mine. This Court finds that the adjustment of the exploration block scope of Wangjiaba Coal Mine was made in 2020. However, at the time of the overlay occurrence in 2011, the coordinates of the N4065 tower foundation were still within the exploration block of Wangjiaba Coal Mine, and Southern Grid Ultra-high Voltage Company had no disagreement on this fact. Therefore, at the time the overlay occurred, Wangjiaba Coal Mine's exploration right covered the mineral resources within the scope of the N4065 tower foundation. Southern Grid Ultra-high Voltage Company, by relying on the current exploration block scope of Wangjiaba Coal Mine, denies the compensation claim brought by Wangjiaba Coal Industry based on the exploration right it enjoyed at the time of the overlay in 2011. This Court does not support this argument.

In conclusion, the appellate claims of both Wangjiaba Coal Industry and Southern Grid Ultra-high Voltage Company cannot be sustained and shall be dismissed. The judgment of first instance has clear findings of fact and correct application of law, and shall be affirmed. Pursuant to Item (1) of Paragraph 1 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

The appeals are dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The case acceptance fee for the second instance, amounting to RMB 59,431.25, shall be borne by Guizhou Huading Wangjiaba Coal Industry Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 49,562.96 and by China Southern Power Grid Co., Ltd., Ultra-high Voltage Transmission Company in the amount of RMB 9,868.29.

This judgment is final.
